# Latency

**Latency** refers to the time delay between the initiation of an operation and
its completion. In Java applications, latency often arises when threads are
forced to wait for external resources or system operations to complete. For
example, when a method performs I/O operations such as reading from a file,
querying a database, or calling a remote service, the executing thread may be
blocked until the data is returned. This waiting period contributes directly to
the method’s latency. The more time a thread spends blocked or idle, the higher
the observed latency for that operation.

Latency is especially important in performance-critical applications, where
responsiveness and throughput are key. High latency can be caused by slow
external systems, inefficient code, resource contention, or poor thread
management. Minimizing latency often involves using asynchronous programming
models, optimizing I/O operations, or leveraging non-blocking APIs to keep
threads available and responsive.

In this example, the program reads text from multiple files and appends the
content of each to a shared list. The order of the lines is unimportant, and the
contents of different files may be interleaved in the list; they do not need to
be stored as contiguous blocks. The original implementation uses multiple
threads and synchronisation (`synchronized`) to protect the shared list.
However, this causes significant contention, as only one thread can write at a
time while others wait. The example is then refactored to first reduce, and
ultimately eliminate, this contention.

## Refactor

1. Reduce the number of calls to the synchronized block.

   Instead of invoking the `addName()` method for every line, we can read all
   lines from each file and then add all lines at one go.

   Copy the updated code from the `fixtures/01-reduced-contention/` directory.

   ```shell
   rsync --archive 'fixtures/01-reduced-contention/' .
   ```

   The [`ReadNames` class](./src/main/java/demo/ReadNames.java) should look like
   the following example.

   ```java
   package demo;

   import java.io.BufferedReader;
   import java.io.IOException;
   import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
   import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
   import java.nio.file.Files;
   import java.nio.file.Path;
   import java.util.ArrayList;
   import java.util.List;
   import java.util.concurrent.CompletionService;
   import java.util.concurrent.ExecutionException;
   import java.util.concurrent.ExecutorCompletionService;
   import java.util.concurrent.ExecutorService;
   import java.util.concurrent.Executors;
   import java.util.stream.Stream;

   public final class ReadNames {

       private final List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();

       public ReadNames read(final Path directory) { /* Closed for brevity */ }

       private Path readNamesFromFile(final Path file) {
           final List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();
           try (BufferedReader reader = Files.newBufferedReader(file, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
               for (String line; (line = reader.readLine()) != null; ) {
                   names.add(line);
               }
           } catch (final IOException e) {
               throw new UncheckedIOException("Failed to read names from file: %s".formatted(file), e);
           }

           addNames(names);

           return file;
       }

       private static List<Path> listFiles(final Path directory) { /* Closed for brevity */ }

       private synchronized void addNames(final List<String> names) {
           this.names.addAll(names);
       }

       public synchronized int size() { /* Closed for brevity */ }
   }
   ```

5. This can be improved even further by removing the need to synchronize at all.

   Copy the updated code from the `fixtures/02-no-contention/` directory.

   ```shell
   rsync --archive 'fixtures/02-no-contention/' .
   ```

   The [`ReadNames` class](./src/main/java/demo/ReadNames.java) should look like
   the following example.

   ```java
   package demo;

   import java.io.BufferedReader;
   import java.io.IOException;
   import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
   import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
   import java.nio.file.Files;
   import java.nio.file.Path;
   import java.util.ArrayList;
   import java.util.List;
   import java.util.concurrent.CompletionService;
   import java.util.concurrent.ExecutionException;
   import java.util.concurrent.ExecutorCompletionService;
   import java.util.concurrent.ExecutorService;
   import java.util.concurrent.Executors;
   import java.util.stream.Stream;

   public final class ReadNames {

       private final List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();

       public ReadNames read(final Path directory) {
           final List<Path> files = listFiles(directory);

           try (ExecutorService executor = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(files.size())) {
               final CompletionService<List<String>> completionService = new ExecutorCompletionService<>(executor);
               files.forEach(file -> completionService.submit(() -> readNamesFromFile(file)));

               for (int i = 0; i < files.size(); i++) {
                   try {
                       final List<String> names = completionService.take().get();
                       this.names.addAll(names);
                   } catch (final InterruptedException e) {
                       Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
                       throw new RuntimeException("Interrupted while waiting for result", e);
                   } catch (final ExecutionException e) {
                       throw new RuntimeException("Failed to read from file", e);
                   }
               }
           }

           return this;
       }

       private static List<String> readNamesFromFile(final Path file) {
           final List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();
           try (BufferedReader reader = Files.newBufferedReader(file, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
               for (String line; (line = reader.readLine()) != null; ) {
                   names.add(line);
               }
           } catch (final IOException e) {
               throw new UncheckedIOException("Failed to read names from file: %s".formatted(file), e);
           }

           return names;
       }

       private static List<Path> listFiles(final Path directory) {
           try (Stream<Path> stream = Files.list(directory)) {
               return stream.toList();
           } catch (IOException e) {
               throw new UncheckedIOException("Failed to list files in directory: %s".formatted(directory), e);
           }
       }

       public int size() {
           return this.names.size();
       }
   }
   ```

9. Analyse the recording file (`./jfr/demo-before-fix.jfr`) with a custom
   program

   A Java program can open a JFR recording file, analyse each event, and
   identify the methods where lock contention occurs. The example below reads
   the recording file, filters for `jdk.JavaMonitorEnter` events, and counts how
   frequently each method appears. Methods with higher frequencies are likely
   experiencing lock contention.

   ```java
   #!/usr/bin/env -S java --source 25

   import module java.base;
   import module jdk.jfr;

   public static void main(final String[] args) {
       if (args.length < 1 || args.length > 2) {
           System.err.println("Usage: java PrintLockContention <RECORDING-FILE> [<METHOD-REGEX>]");
           System.exit(1);
       }

       final Path path = Path.of(args[0]);
       final Predicate<String> predicate = createPredicateFromArgs(args);
       final Map<String, Long> results = compute(path, predicate);

       results.entrySet().stream()
               .sorted(Map.Entry.<String, Long>comparingByValue().reversed())
               .limit(20)
               .forEach(entry -> System.out.printf("%5d - %s%n", entry.getValue(), entry.getKey()));
   }

   private static Map<String, Long> compute(final Path path, final Predicate<String> predicate) {
       final Map<String, Long> results = new HashMap<>();

       try (RecordingFile recordingFile = new RecordingFile(path)) {
           while (recordingFile.hasMoreEvents()) {
               final RecordedEvent event = recordingFile.readEvent();

               if ("jdk.JavaMonitorEnter".equals(event.getEventType().getName())) {

                   final String method = formatStack(event.getStackTrace());

                   if (predicate.test(method)) {
                       /* The time the thread spent waiting to acquire the monitor. */
                       final long durationNanos = event.getDuration().toNanos();
                       results.merge(method, durationNanos, Long::sum);
                   }
               }
           }

           return results;
       } catch (final IOException e) {
           throw new UncheckedIOException("Failed to read recording file " + path, e);
       }
   }

   private static String formatStack(final RecordedStackTrace stackTrace) {
       if (stackTrace == null || stackTrace.getFrames().isEmpty()) {
           return "Unknown (stack trace is not available)";
       }

       return formatFrame(stackTrace.getFrames().getFirst());
   }

   private static String formatFrame(final RecordedFrame frame) {
       final RecordedMethod method = frame.getMethod();
       return method.getType().getName() + "." + method.getName() + ":" + frame.getLineNumber();
   }

   private static Predicate<String> createPredicateFromArgs(final String[] args) {
       return args.length == 2
               ? Pattern.compile(args[1]).asMatchPredicate()
               : t -> true;
   }
   ```

   As we are only interested in our own code, the output will include only
   methods belonging to our classes.

   ```shell
   './tools/PrintLockContention' './jfr/demo-before-fix.jfr' 'demo\..*'
   ```

   The program will display methods from classes in the `demo` package where
   threads were blocked waiting for the monitor to become available.

   ```
   17623641226 - demo.ReadNames.addName:65
   ```

   Let us now compare the sample counts from the second recording, taken after
   the fix was applied.

   ```shell
   './tools/PrintLockContention' './jfr/demo-after-fix-1.jfr' 'demo\..*'
   ```

   The program will display methods from classes in the `demo` package where
   threads were blocked waiting for the monitor to become available.

   ```
   3675965689 - demo.ReadNames.addNames:68
   ```

   Note that the time spent waiting by each thread has dropped but not
   eliminated. Let us now compare the sample counts from the third recording,
   taken after the contention was eliminated.

   ```shell
   './tools/PrintLockContention' './jfr/demo-after-fix-2.jfr' 'demo\..*'
   ```

   This time, the programme prints nothing as no threads are blocked waiting.
